title: Zassenhaus Butterfly Lemma for Subgroups (Schreier Refinement Engine)
problemStatement: Formalize the Zassenhaus butterfly lemma (Schmetterlingslemma, 1934) for subgroups in Lean 4 / Mathlib: for A ⊴ A' and B ⊴ B', the two tower quotients A(A'∩B')/A(A'∩B) and B(B'∩A')/B(B'∩A) are isomorphic, both being isomorphic to the common middle quotient (A'∩B')/((A∩B')(A'∩B)). This is the combinatorial engine behind Schreier's refinement theorem and is not yet in Mathlib (identified as a gap in OQ-04, the Jordan-Hölder formalization).

insights: The full butterfly reduces to a SINGLE 'half' isomorphism U_A/L_A ≃* I/M (I = A'∩B', M = (A∩B')⊔(A'∩B)); the second tower is the same lemma with A↔B swapped, and the butterfly follows by composing through the common middle quotient via symmetry/transitivity of the iso relation. This reduction (zassenhaus_butterfly) is written and, modulo the half-iso, needs only inf_comm/sup_comm rewrites (middle_symm, inter_symm).

Mathlib now HAS the Dedekind modular law (the historical blocker): Subgroup.mul_inf_assoc / Subgroup.inf_mul_assoc give ↑A * ↑(B ⊓ C) = ↑A * ↑B ∩ ↑C for A ≤ C. Applying inf_mul_assoc with A'⊓B ≤ A'⊓B' computes the kernel of the surjection as exactly M = (A∩B')⊔(A'∩B).

The half-iso is provable by the SAME technique OQ-04 used for Noether's second_iso: build φ = mk' ∘ inclusion : (A'⊓B') →* U_A ⧸ L_A.subgroupOf U_A, show surjectivity via mem_sup + relative normality of A in A', and identify ker φ = M via the Dedekind law; then QuotientGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective.

M ⊴ I is fully provable: A∩B' and A'∩B are each normal in A'∩B' (restrictions of A ⊴ A' and B ⊴ B' via normal_subgroupOf_of_le_normalizer), and a join of normal subgroups is normal (subgroupOf_sup + instance).
